plan.title: Completed-write guard rejects canonical completion after mutable brief changes

narratives.Description: verify:completed-write-guard still pairs a stamped complete to its deleted active source by four-part planIdentity, so a legitimate complete after item-title or narrative movement is refused as unpaired. The bound recut pairs when pairingKey, plan.title, origin issue refs, and a valid complete stamp match, including persist-on-complete and HEAD recovery, while copied stamps with a different title or origin still fail closed.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary
On Directive **0.119.3**, `scope:complete` can successfully move an already-delivered scope from `active/` to `completed/` and write a valid canonical transition stamp, yet `verify:completed-write-guard` rejects the same change as an active deletion with no paired stamped destination.

The pairing identity contains mutable item titles and the entire narratives object. When an active brief is legitimately updated before completion, the deleted source recovered from Git can differ from the stamped destination even though this is the same scope and canonical transition.

This report concerns a **false refusal of a stamped transition**, not missing stamps, invalid disposition evidence, or permission to delete an unrelated brief.

## Observed consumer flow
- Consumer: [deftai/BestiMax#357](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/issues/357), delivered through [PR #376](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/pull/376).
- Environment: macOS/zsh; installed `@deftai/directive-core`, CLI, and vendored content all at **0.119.3**.
- Verified delivery merge: `ad05e634a8a323dd5d52a813d0fe73231e201284`, ancestor of both worktree HEAD and `origin/develop`.
- Before final completion, earlier local repairs added a `LifecycleRepair` narrative and three pending synthetic clause items generated by the completion path. Existing clause evidence was then attached to the matching items; statuses were not manually pre-marked completed.
- The final `scope:complete` command alone moved the file and advanced all seven items.

Observed commands and results:

```sh
deft scope:complete -- xbrief/active/2026-09-16-357-highlight-what-changed-between-quote-versions.xbrief.json \
  --merge-commit ad05e634a8a323dd5d52a813d0fe73231e201284 --pr 376
# exit 0

deft verify:orphan-active --issue 357
# exit 0

deft verify:completed-write-guard --base-ref origin/develop
# exit 1
```

Exact guard finding:

```text
verify_completed_write_guard: 1 finding(s) (#3679 / #3766).
  - xbrief/active/2026-09-16-357-highlight-what-changed-between-quote-versions.xbrief.json: deleted from active/ with no paired stamped destination
Halt: run `task scope:complete` or `task scope:cancel` so the destination is stamped, or leave the brief untracked. Lone-D untracking cleanup is not an authorization token (#3766).
```

The completed artifact has `plan.status = completed`, seven terminal items, and:

```json
{
  "lifecycleWrite": {
    "action": "complete",
    "writtenAt": "2026-09-18T16:18:58Z"
  }
}
```

Targeted completed-folder consistency, `validateBriefForPersist`, transition-write presence, and stamp/folder agreement checks pass. The real source and destination have matching plan titles and issue references; their item-title lists and narratives differ from HEAD.

## Isolated verifier reproduction
Using the installed 0.119.3 `evaluateCompletedWriteGuard(projectRoot, {nameStatus, payloads})` test seams, I ran eight in-memory probes without writing repository files or Git state:

1. Source `xbrief/active/repro.xbrief.json`: running plan, stable `plan.id = github.issue.123`, one canonical issue reference, one narrative, and one pending item.
2. Destination `xbrief/completed/repro.xbrief.json`: clone the same source, set plan/item status to completed, and supply a fixture `metadata.lifecycleWrite` with action `complete` and a valid timestamp.
3. Inject source and destination JSON through `payloads`. This isolates the identity comparison; the fixture stamp is **not** claimed to come from a fresh `scope:complete` run. The real consumer run above provides that evidence.
4. Evaluate both `D <source> + A <destination>` and `R100 <source> <destination>` name-status shapes.
5. Repeat with exactly one extra difference in the destination.

Measured results for **both** diff shapes:
- No mutable-content change: **0**.
- Add only `narratives.LifecycleRepair`: **1**, unpaired stamped destination.
- Change only an existing item title: **1**, same refusal.
- Add only one item: **1**, same refusal.

The added-item fixture used schema-safe ID `clause_1`; the failure does not depend on the separate `clause:1` ID-format defect. The stable plan ID, issue reference, and transition stamp stay identical across each control/failing pair.

## Code-level cause
Relevant module: `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-write-guard.ts`; verified against the installed 0.119.3 compiled counterpart:
- `planIdentity` combines plan title, issue references, ordered item titles, and `JSON.stringify(plan.narratives)` (installed JS lines 95–118). It does not use `plan.id`.
- `sourceIdentity` recovers the deleted source from `HEAD:<source>` first, then other Git history/base candidates (lines 439–477).
- Both deletion/addition and rename pairing require exact identity equality (lines 483–496).

The guard already discovers untracked additions. **Staging the destination alone is not the remedy**, and changing `--base-ref` does not supersede an available source from HEAD. The diagnostic recommends the completion command that has already succeeded.

## Expected behavior and regression boundary
- A legitimate, canonical stamped transition must remain recognizable after supported updates to an active brief, including added lifecycle/evidence notes and generated acceptance items.
- Cover both deletion/addition and rename discovery, including an untracked destination and the source recovered from Git history.
- Preserve the protection from #3766: unrelated deletions, swapped destinations, missing or wrong-folder stamps, and ambiguous scope identity must still fail closed.
- If a content change genuinely prevents authorization, report that mismatch and a usable recovery rather than asserting no stamped destination exists.
- Do not require discarding truthful evidence or weakening the guard to complete the consumer flow. The appropriate identity/transition-proof design is for maintainer review; simply dropping content checks is not the proposed fix.

## Impact and limits
The local lifecycle transition succeeded, but its change set cannot pass the write guard. No supported evidence-preserving recovery was found within the authorized no-commit boundary. No real index changes, commits, pushes, policy changes, or guard edits were used to force a pass.

The separate `verify:completed-tracked` failure is expected while the completed artifact is unpublished on `origin/develop`; this report does not ask to weaken that publication check. Unrelated historical conformance errors are also outside this report.

## Deduplication
Searched open and closed Directive issues for `completed-write-guard`, `paired stamped`, `planIdentity`, and narrative/identity/clause variants, and reviewed the closest bodies and comment threads:
- #3766: unauthorized active deletion with no legitimate destination; the protection this false-positive repair must preserve.
- #4508: reconcile omitted the transition stamp. Here canonical completion wrote it.
- #4001: reconcile routes superseded proposals to the wrong terminal folder.
- #3819: disposition validation and modified completed artifacts, not mutable-content transition pairing.
- #4119: stable `plan.id` production/admission. A comment mentions the existing content-based `planIdentity`, but the bound scope is minting/admission/repair, not this guard's false refusal.
- #4732: binding clauses and stamping test-axis evidence before completion.
- #4707: generated clause IDs versus schema validation; independently excluded by the schema-safe in-memory reproduction.

No existing issue found covers this exact false-positive mechanism.

Refs #1709.

## Gate stamp

P1 is the false refusal of a canonical stamped complete after supported mutable-content updates to the active brief (added LifecycleRepair narrative, changed item titles, added generated acceptance items) while plan.id, issue references, folder move, and lifecycleWrite.action=complete stay identical. Consumer: deftai/BestiMax#357 / PR #376 on Directive 0.119.3. scope:complete exited 0; verify:orphan-active exited 0; verify:completed-write-guard exited 1 with deleted from active/ with no paired stamped destination. Isolated evaluateCompletedWriteGuard probes at 0.119.3: no mutable-content change pairs (0 findings); add LifecycleRepair, change one item title, or add one item each refuse (1 finding) on both D+A and R100 shapes.

Pin-read at dispatch-sha f33b8b8e24c9746d02f66532bd1815271771e969:

- packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-write-guard.ts planIdentity (164-169) concatenates plan.title, originIssueKey (issue refs), itemTitles, and narrativesIdentity (JSON.stringify(plan.narratives)). It does not read plan.id.
- D+A pairing (589-591) requires pairingKey match and dest.identity === srcId. Rename pairing (585-587) requires dest.identity === srcId. Both are exact string equality on that composite.
- sourceIdentity (539-572) recovers the deleted source from the working tree, then HEAD:src, then git history / base-ref. Staging the destination alone does not change that comparison.
- Halt copy (#3766): no paired stamped destination. Unrelated deletions, swapped destinations, missing or wrong-folder stamps must still fail closed.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased at this SHA has no completed-write-guard identity recut. Tests at completed-write-guard.test.ts do not name planIdentity or a mutable-title/narrative pair that still shares plan.id.

Inventory already on the tree: #3766 unpaired-deletion protection; #4508 omitted stamp (this path wrote the stamp); #4119 plan.id mint/admission (comment mentions content-based planIdentity; bound scope is not this guard); #3819 modified completed artifacts; #4732 clause binding before complete. Do not invent dropping content checks as the fix. No implement and no ingest from this parent.

The recorded refutation-target holds. Pairing a stamped complete to its deleted active source requires exact `planIdentity` equality over title + github-issue URIs + ordered item titles + `JSON.stringify(narratives)`, and that equality is why a stamped dest whose identity-bearing fields moved is reported as unpaired.

Re-verification at dispatch SHA `f33b8b8e24c9746d02f66532bd1815271771e969`:

- `planIdentity` (completed-write-guard.ts:164-169) joins those four parts and does not read `plan.id`, `plan.status`, item status, or `metadata.lifecycleWrite`.
- Rename pairing (585-587) and D+A pairing (589-591) both require `dest.identity === srcId`.
- Isolated pairing probes (same `nameStatus` + `payloads` shape as the issue): no identity-bearing change pairs on both D+A and R100 (0 findings). Add `narratives.LifecycleRepair`, change one item title, or add one `clause_1` item: 1 finding on both shapes, halt copy "no paired stamped destination". Item-status-only complete still pairs (0).
- `plan.id` dest `github.issue.999` vs source `github.issue.123` with matching identity fields: 0 findings. Matching `plan.id` with different narratives: 1 finding.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased at this SHA has no completed-write-guard identity recut.
- Existing tests call `evaluateCompletedWriteGuard` and already lock "same-title dest whose plan.items titles differ" and "same-title dest whose narratives differ" as code 1.

Dest had no `node_modules`, so the numeric probes executed a verbatim extract of `planIdentity` plus the D/R pairing loop from that pin-read, not a live import of `evaluateCompletedWriteGuard`. The existing tests above are the live-evaluator corroboration of the same refusals.

## 1. Published D+A extra-check is title; implementation is full planIdentity

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `content/commands.md` `verify:completed-write-guard` and the in-file comment at completed-write-guard.ts:473-475 say D+A also requires dest `plan.title` to match so a copied stamp cannot authorize an unrelated brief. The code path those sentences describe is `dest.identity === srcId` on the four-part composite. Tests at completed-write-guard.test.ts:353-387 encode item-title and narrative mismatch as intended #3766 refusals, not as missing coverage. They do not name `planIdentity` or a shared-`plan.id` pair that must still pass.

Failure mode: a bound remedy that "keep the current pairing rule, just add plan.id" and a bound remedy that "restore the published title-only extra-check" are different contracts. The second would red those two tests. The first would keep refusing LifecycleRepair / generated clause titles.

Disposition consequence: the successor lean must name which pairing rule is being bound — published title-match, or the tested four-part identity — before ingest. The recorded target is true of the code either way; it is not yet a choice between those two rules.

## 2. Canonical complete can mint the item-title mismatch in the same verb

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `runTransition` for `complete` calls `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems` (transition.ts:338-345) before the folder move. That helper pushes `{ id, title: id, status: "pending" }` for each unbound acceptance clause (`clauseKeyedItemId`, acceptance-evidence.ts:414-415, 646-650) and may write those items onto the active source. `sourceIdentity` (539-572) then reads the working-tree source if present, else `HEAD:src` / history / base-ref. After a successful move the working-tree source is gone, so the recovered identity is the last committed active blob.

Failure mode: a complete that generates clause-keyed items in-run (the issue's "three pending synthetic clause items generated by the completion path") produces dest item titles that `HEAD:src` does not have, even when the operator never edited titles or narratives as a separate pre-complete change. Framing the pain as only "supported mutable-content updates before completion" would let a remedy special-case operator edits and still false-refuse persist-on-complete.

Disposition consequence: scope the bound pain to include in-run persist + HEAD recovery, not only pre-complete working-tree edits. A snapshot-recovery recut without thinning `planIdentity` would also address this; a content-thinning recut that ignores persist would not.

## 3. Pairing identity is the deletion-authorization token

sharpens-framing

Evidence: authorized dests are stamped completed/cancelled adds; D+A then requires `pairingKey` (family/basename) and `dest.identity === srcId`. The #3766 test "rejects a copied stamp under the same basename with a different title" is that authorization check. Dest JSON is contributor-controlled (the guard already byte-caps completed/ reads). `extractPlanId` exists in scope-provenance/parent-lineage and is unused here.

Failure mode: collapsing pairing to `pairingKey` + stamp lets a same-basename copied stamp with a matching title authorize an unrelated deletion (items/narratives/issue URIs would no longer distinguish). Collapsing to `plan.id` alone lets dest JSON copy the victim's id. The recorded target is why legitimate completes miss; this is why dropping the content parts is not a free recut.

Disposition consequence: any identity recut stays an authorization recut. Keep a dest-cannot-self-authorize-unrelated-deletion control. Do not treat `plan.id` mint/admission (#4119) as already doing that job in this guard.

## 4. D+A also requires pairingKey

footnote

Same-identity dest under a different basename (`xbrief/completed/other.xbrief.json`) still unpaired (1 finding, identities equal). Necessary identity equality is not sufficient for D+A. This consumer path is same-basename, so it does not explain the reported refusal.

## 5. JSON.stringify is key-order identity

footnote

Semantically equal narratives `{Overview, LifecycleRepair}` vs `{LifecycleRepair, Overview}` refuse (1 finding). Omitted `narratives` vs `{}` also refuse. The target already names `JSON.stringify`; this is the serialize-order consequence, not a second pairing rule.

## Road not taken

Rejected refutation: pairing is title-only as commands.md and the in-file comment say, so the target misstates the rule. Steelman: if those sentences were the operative predicate, the four-part equality would be an implementation accident and the false refusal would be "code overshot the published extra-check," not "pairing requires planIdentity." Flip: `dest.identity === srcId` would compare title only. Pin-read 587/591 compare the composite; the eight mutation probes follow that composite, not title.
